paper_title: An analysis of vaccine-related sentiments from development to deployment   of COVID-19 vaccines
caption: : Caption not extracted
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the distribution of sentiment polarity scores for vaccine-related text, with the x-axis representing “Polarity scores” ranging from –1.0 to 0.6 in linear increments of 0.2, and the y-axis representing “Counts” ranging from 0 to 50,000 in linear increments of 10,000. A single blue line with circular markers connects data points, showing a low and relatively flat count near zero for strongly negative polarity scores (from –1.0 to –0.8), followed by a gradual rise to approximately 5,000 at –0.6. The count then dips slightly before rising sharply to a peak of nearly 50,000 at a polarity score of 0.0. After this peak, the count declines steeply to about 18,000 at 0.1, rises again to roughly 28,000 at 0.2, then drops to 9,000 at 0.3, falls further to near 0 at 0.4, climbs to about 10,000 at 0.5, and ends at approximately 1,000 at 0.6. The plot suggests a strong concentration of sentiment around neutral polarity (0.0), with decreasing frequency as polarity becomes more positive or negative.
